summary: Start a safe, masked API-key wizard on an interactive credential-less bare invocation and through auth setup; use terminal ioctls so redirected character devices do not prompt; keep machine, help, and version paths non-blocking.
reason: The generated CLI had a private credential store and a direct token-argument command, but its bare command only printed help and setup told users to put a token in their shell history. This local product requirement needs a guided first-run path that reuses SaveTokens and its existing private-file permission safeguards, removes direct token-argument entry, and replaces stale guidance. The generated tree does not provide this routing, real-terminal detection, masked terminal input, or PTY coverage for that flow.
validated_outcome: Focused CLI auth tests, go vet ./internal/cli, go build ./cmd/kie-pp-cli, and Linux and Windows test-binary cross-compiles pass. PTY subprocess tests prove bare first-run setup masks entry, saves a reusable credential, and avoids prompts for /dev/null input on both bare and auth setup routes. A real local terminal session captured with a fake key supplies the README screenshot.
